subject: Request: Priority Queue Exemption and Throughput Smoothing (Hyperswitch)
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@hyperswitch.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hyperswitch.io
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary priority queue exemption for reserved pool

Hi Grace / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile and logging make Redwood a strong candidate for our inference tier. We have one operational constraint that could block the go/no-go for our reserved pool order: during our daily batch window (03:00–04:30 UTC) Hyperswitch runs a short-lived spike of high-concurrency classification requests that produce many small, low-latency inferences. Those spikes push other teams' production traffic into tail queueing and we need a short-term guarantee that the reserved pool won't degrade these mission-critical spikes by more than 10% in p95 latency.

Specifically we are requesting: a temporary "priority queue exemption" for the first 90 days after reservation activation that (a) grants Hyperswitch a soft-priority token allocation during our scheduled batch window, and (b) allows Redwood to use throughput-smoothing (burst shaping) rather than strict FIFO queueing to keep tails bounded.

We understand this may be an exception from standard dedicated-pool SLAs. To move forward quickly, could you:
- Confirm whether Redwood supports soft-priority tokens or a token-bucket carving approach for reserved GPUs
- Share a proposal for how queueing would behave during overlapping peaks (example: cap on preemptive tokens, fallback to compatible model variant)
- Tell us what observable metrics you can expose for the first 30 days so we can validate impact (per-route p50/p95/p99, queue depth, token spend)

I've attached a short form with our window and traffic shape, and a small observability sample from last Tuesday to help size the ask. If this looks doable I'd like to align on wording for the order so procurement can proceed.

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP, Platform Engineering
Hyperswitch

[Attachment: priority_q_exemption_form.pdf]
[Attachment: observability_dump-20260112.log]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@hyperswitch.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary priority queue exemption for reserved pool

Hi Sanjay — appreciated the data and clear ask. Short answer: we can discuss a temporary priority allocation pattern for a reserved pool, but there are a few constraints we'll need to make explicit so the impact is contained and our SLAs remain predictable for other customers.

High-level items we need to align on:
- Scope & duration: you asked 90 days; we typically do 30–60 day trials for exceptions and instrument closely. Can you confirm if 30 days with an option to extend to 90 based on metrics would work?
- Guarantee boundaries: our commercial SLAs are uptime + throughput. Any preemptive token allocation would be soft (non-preemptive for live non-Hyperswitch traffic) and capped to avoid starve conditions.
- Observability: we can provide a dedicated dashboard stream (per-route p50/p95/p99, queue depth, token accounting) and daily digest for the trial window.
- Fallback policy: when headroom is exhausted the system will gracefully route to a compatible lower-cost model variant or spill to a burst pool if available — we need to confirm acceptable degradation modes with you.

Looping in Lauren from runtime so she can weigh in on the technical controls and a concrete proposal for queue behavior. Aditya — can you please prepare a commercial note about trial billing (credits, ramp) that we can attach to the SOW?

I'll draft a short technical proposal and proposed SOW language after Lauren confirms the implementation approach.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@hyperswitch.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary priority queue exemption for reserved pool

Thanks for the context — I've reviewed the observability dump and sketched an implementation pattern that balances your spike isolation need with our tenant fairness model. Summary:

- Mechanism: "soft reservation tokens" (per-minute token bucket) allocated to Hyperswitch during the agreed window. Tokens buy priority scheduling up to a capped rate; when exhausted traffic falls back to normal scheduling. Tokens are counted against a trial allowance.
- Throttling: we'll enforce a cap of 15% of pool concurrency as soft-priority tokens during the window to avoid starvation. That cap can be tuned after the trial's first week.
- Smoothing: rather than strict FIFO preemption, we will use throughput-smoothing with a 30s lookback (moving average) to dampen spikes and avoid large queue oscillations.
- Observability: we'll stream per-route token spend, queue depth, and p95 latency to a customer dashboard (30s granularity) and export daily CSVs for your telemetry team.
- Fallbacks: 1) spill to a previously-agreed burst pool (if purchased), 2) route to a compatible quantized variant (3-bit quant) with documented quality delta, 3) degraded throughput with graceful backoff.

Caveats & next steps:
- This requires a short SRE runbook and 24/7 on-call monitoring for the trial start (first 72 hours). Redwood can provide 8 hours/day coverage and an on-call escalation if you need continuous coverage (add-on).
- We need procurement sign-off on a trial credit structure (Aditya) and Hyperswitch confirmation it accepts the documented fallback quality delta for the quantized variant.

If this approach looks okay I'll produce a one-page technical appendix we can append to the SOW. Sanjay — are you available Wed 14 Jan at 10:00 PT for a quick alignment call?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary priority queue exemption for reserved pool

Grace/Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the concrete plan, this looks actionable. We can accept a 30-day trial with option to extend to 90 based on the metrics you listed. A few clarifications before the call:

- 15% cap: acceptable as a starting point. Can you include a short escalation path if we see persistent degradation after week 1?
- Observability: the 30s granularity CSV export is fine. Please add per-request model-variant tag so we can measure quality deltas for the quantized fallbacks.
- On-call coverage: we'll take the 8 hours/day Redwood coverage and add a Hyperswitch runbook contact for overnight.

We'll sign the SOW addendum once Aditya confirms the credit structure. Wed 14 Jan 10:00 PT works — sending calendar invite now.

Thanks,
Sanjay Mehta
VP, Platform Engineering
Hyperswitch
